state.question: Why do my four independent measurement streams show near-zero or weakly negative cross-correlations at various time lags, when I would expect either strong agreement (if they measure the same quantity) or clear independence (if they measure different ones)? And why do individual instruments show weak or negative autocorrelations with their own past readings?

hypotheses.label: Calibration drift or thermal/mechanical instability in instruments
hypotheses.rationale: Weak autocorrelations in all four streams (pendulum_lab -0.421, resonator_lab -0.294, pendulum_obs -0.168, resonator_obs 0.250) suggest systematic noise or real drift rather than random error. If each instrument drifts independently on a 3–6 day cycle, readings would decorrelate from their own past and show weak cross-correlations. Day 10 readings (events 523891–481279) cluster plausibly within baseline variance, but I have no post-baseline data yet to detect drift. This is testable and fits the pattern of weak but not random structure.

hypotheses.label: My cross-check correlations are artifacts of small sample sizes and multiple comparisons
hypotheses.rationale: All cross-correlations are weak (range -0.490 to 0.382) and most fall within or near their chance-level thresholds (e.g., pendulum_lab ↔ pendulum_obs: -0.342 vs ±0.483 chance).
